html:
Umar Tall was a West African Muslim scholar and leader of the Tijaniyya Sufi order who, from 1852 until his death in 1864, conquered an empire on the upper Senegal and Niger rivers, the Toucouleur Empire.

Born around 1797 in Futa Toro, in today's Senegal, he made the pilgrimage to Mecca in the late 1820s and came home as the Tijaniyya order's leader for West Africa. He gathered followers, bought guns, and in 1852 declared jihad against non-Muslim rulers and Muslims he judged lax.

  • 1854 to 1855: conquered Kaarta.
  • 1857: failed to take the French fort at Medine on the Senegal, held by the soldiers of French Senegal, and turned east.
  • 1861: took Ségou, capital of the Bamana kingdom of Ségou.
  • 1862: took Hamdullahi, capital of the Muslim Massina Empire, a war of Muslims on Muslims that turned many against him.

Massina rose in revolt and besieged him. In 1864 he died in a cave near Bandiagara, in an explosion of gunpowder, while trying to escape. His son Ahmadu ruled from Ségou until the French took it in 1890.
sum: Umar Tall was a West African Muslim scholar and leader of the Tijaniyya Sufi order who, from 1852 until his death in 1864, conquered an empire on the upper Senegal and Niger rivers, the Toucouleur Empire.
